paper.title: Modeling civil violence: An agent-based computational approach

headline: Epstein 2002 civil violence (agent-based, Model I): 3/3 locked clauses REPRO; L=0.9 mean active 0.000, L=0.5 mean active 0.108 / burstiness 6.40, cop-sweep 0.375->0.108->0.059

verdicts.gate: P1 high legitimacy (L=0.9) -> calm (mean active fraction < 0.05)
P2 low legitimacy (L=0.5) -> punctuated (burstiness>=5 OR mean active>=0.10)
P3 deterrence: mean active fraction monotonically non-increasing in cop density

extra.scope: faithful reproduction of a published synthetic model; no real-world data; the contribution is whether the harness + lock-first discipline reproduce the punctuated-rebellion / legitimacy / deterrence results and would catch an artifact

citations: Epstein, J.M. (2002). Modeling civil violence: An agent-based computational approach. PNAS 99(suppl 3):7243-7250. doi:10.1073/pnas.092080199. Open: https://www.pnas.org/doi/10.1073/pnas.092080199

benchmark.note: no cross-tool baseline; faithful single-implementation reproduction
